While those advances allow the construction of more accurate models, hidden quantity inference and model testing are now often done approximately. This raises questions as to how it impacts the Popperian falsification procedure. Can a model or hidden quantities be reliably refuted by an approximate inference or testing procedure? It could be that our procedure leads to refutation only because of approximations and that if that same procedure was applied without approximations, refutation could not be obtained. Incorrect refutation of models could then ultimately prevent scientists from exploring valid models and lead them in the wrong direction. In this thesis, we aim to adapt modern scientific reasoning to take into account the approx- imations made. At the root of this adapted methodology is the inclusion of the additional source of uncertainty brought by those approximations. Statistical methods are modified to produce inflated uncertainty estimates based on how the approximations are likely to affect the end result. In particular, we argue that underestimating the uncertainty is more harmful than overestimating it for Popperian falsification. Indeed, underestimation of un- certainty can lead to incorrect refutation, while overestimation can only lead to failing to refute a model. With this in mind, we design new statistical methods to try to avoid under- estimation of the uncertainty and, hence, overconfidence. These methods can then be used more reliably for scientific analyses, and more trust can be given to conclusions drawn. We focus on models that take the form of a simulator. ## #1 Inference After Model Refutation: Uniform Post-Relaxation Inference for Partially Identified Models [PDF] [Copy] [Kimi] [REL]

When data reject an econometric model, the researcher must decide which identifying assumptions to give up. If several equally preferred repairs restore compatibility, the repair itself is unknown, and inference under any one of them can exclude structural values supported by the others, even when that inference is exact. I propose Post-Relaxation Projection (PR), which carries one simultaneous confidence event through every repair that may be minimal. With repair-by-repair primitive bounds, PR equals the union of all post-relaxation targets compatible with the band, so no smaller band-based set has the same guarantee. I derive limits on learning the repair, the exact perturbation radius of the minimal-repair correspondence, oracle-equivalent adaptation, and a reduced-form version valid at zero first stages. In cross-country data on institutions and income, the data do not settle which historical instrument should be dropped, yet every admissible minimum repair implies a positive effect of institutions.

As discussed in the preceding section, there could exist discordant submodels when the full model is refuted. However, the falsification of the full model does not necessarily lead to discordancy of the submodels. In this section, we will present a sufficient condition which ensures that all data-consistent submodels are always compatible with each other.

To state our result, we need to introduce a new concept. When the full model is refuted, we can get some data-consistent submodel by dropping or relaxing some of the assumptions. We say that a data-consistent submodel is a minimum relaxation if we just relaxed the minimum ammount of assumptions to restore the data consistency.

jina.snippet:
该论文提出了一种名为**后放松投影（Post-Relaxation Projection, PR）**的推理方法，旨在解决当数据拒绝原模型时，研究者因存在多种同等合理的“修复”（Relaxation）方案而面临的不确定性问题。

### 核心背景与问题

在实证研究中，若数据拒绝了主模型，研究者通常会选择弱化假设（即“修复”模型）。如果存在多种先验上同样合理的修复方案（如排除不同的工具变量或矩条件），且每种方案都能使模型与数据兼容，但这些方案对应的结构参数识别集不同，那么“选择一个修复方案再进行推理”的做法会导致失效。论文指出，这种选择步骤本身就是一种不含在目标参数中的约束，会造成严重的推断偏差。

### 核心方法：Post-Relaxation Projection (PR)

PR方法的核心思想是：不进行任何预先的修复选择，而是通过一个**联合置信事件**覆盖所有可能的最小修复方案。

1.   **修复菜单与成本**：研究者在观测数据前定义一组可能的修复方案 $\left{\right. R \left.\right}$，并赋予其先验的科学成本 $c \left(\right. R \left.\right)$。
2.   **最小修复目标**：定义最小 feasible 成本为 $c^{\star} \left(\right. P \left.\right) = \left(min ⁡\right)_{R : \Theta_{R} \left(\right. P \left.\right) = \emptyset} c \left(\right. R \left.\right)$，目标集为所有符合该最小成本的修复方案对应的识别集的并集：

$$
\Theta_{M R} \left(\right. P \left.\right) = \underset{R \in R^{\star} \left(\right. P \left.\right)}{\cup} \Theta_{R} \left(\right. P \left.\right)
$$

3.   **PR 推理构建**：
    *   构建一个关于原始模型参数的**同时置信矩形（Simultaneous Primitive Band）**，涵盖所有修复方案的约束条件及可行性指标 $q_{R} \left(\right. P \left.\right)$。
    *   定义可行性“三明治”规则，根据矩形中的可行性指标判断哪些修复方案在统计上仍有可能是人口意义下的“最小修复”。
    *   PR集合即为在置信区域内所有被认为符合“最小修复”条件的方案所对应的结构外集（Structural Outer Sets）的并集。

### 技术细节与理论成果

*   **信息界限**：作者证明了在局部错定模型下，任何诚实的推理过程都存在一个关于学习最小修复方案的极小极大风险界限。PR方法能够通过矩形信息直接获得目标集的覆盖，且无需估计具体的修复方案。
*   **Bandwise Completeness**：在 canonical 构造下，PR集合恰好是所有与该置信矩形相容的最小修复目标的并集，这意味着该方法在给定的矩形信息下达到了信息最优。
*   **弱工具变量（Weak IV）适应性**：在工具变量模型中，该方法不需要第一阶段相关性（First-stage relevance）的下界，能够在不依赖于第一阶段系数比率的情况下，实现对结构参数的均匀有效覆盖。

keenable.snippet:
# Inference After Model Refutation:
Uniform Post-Relaxation Inference for Partially Identified Models
This version: November 11, 2026
###### Abstract
When data reject a model, the researcher must decide which identifying assumptions to give up. If several equally preferred repairs restore compatibility, the repair itself is unknown, and inference under any one of them can exclude structural values supported by the others. I propose Post-Relaxation Projection (PR), which carries one simultaneous confidence event through every repair that may be minimal. For a rectangular band on the repair-specific restrictions, PR contains exactly the post-relaxation targets compatible with that band. I also derive limits on learning the repair, its exact perturbation radius, oracle-equivalent adaptation, and versions for instrumental variables without a first-stage relevance bound. In cross-country data on institutions and income, the data do not settle which historical instrument to drop, yet every admissible minimum repair implies a positive effect, and the sign survives sizable direct effects of the instruments on income.

Empirical work rarely stops when a maintained model is rejected. The usual response is to weaken it: drop an exclusion restriction, remove a block of moment inequalities, or relax a shape or behavioral restriction. This step is innocuous when one relaxation is clearly the right one. It is not innocuous when several relaxations are judged equally costly on substantive grounds, each is just enough to restore compatibility with the data, and they support different values of the structural parameter. Choosing among them then changes the object being estimated, not only the estimator. In this paper each repair is a candidate relaxation written down before the sample is examined, the repairs are ranked by a scientific order fixed in advance, and the post-refutation target is built from every minimum feasible repair.

Post-Selection Inference for Partially Identified Parameters∗
Sukjin Han†
Adam McCloskey‡
November 16, 2026
Abstract
Partial identification of parameters such as average treatment effects, average partial
effects and welfare is particularly common when using observational data and experimental
data with imperfect compliance due to the endogeneity of individuals’ treatment uptake.
In this setting, the researcher is typically interested in a treatment or policy that is either
selected from the estimated set of best-performers or arises from a data-dependent selection
rule. In this paper, we develop new inference tools for partially-identified parameters chosen
via these forms of selection. We develop three types of confidence intervals for data-dependent
and partially-identified parameters, discuss how they apply to several examples of interest
and prove their uniform asymptotic validity under weak assumptions.

keenable.title: Model-Agnostic Covariate-Assisted Inference on Partially Identified Causal Effects
keenable.snippet: Many causal estimands are only partially identifiable since they depend on the unobservable joint distribution between potential outcomes. Stratification on pretreatment covariates can yield sharper partial identification bounds; however, unless the covariates are discrete with relatively small support, this approach typically requires consistent estimation of the conditional distributions of the potential outcomes given the covariates. Thus, existing approaches may fail under model misspecification or if consistency assumptions are violated. In this study, we propose a unified and model-agnostic inferential approach for a wide class of partially identified estimands, based on duality theory for optimal transport problems. In randomized experiments, our approach can wrap around any estimates of the conditional distributions and provide uniformly valid inference, even if the initial estimates are arbitrarily inaccurate. Also, our approach is doubly robust in observational studies. Notably, this property allows analysts to use the multiplier bootstrap to select covariates and models without sacrificing validity even if the true model is not included. Furthermore, if the conditional distributions are estimated at semiparametric rates, our approach matches the performance of an oracle with perfect knowledge of the outcome model. Finally, we propose an efficient computational framework, enabling implementation on many practical problems in causal inference.

keenable.snippet:
Researchers frequently estimate regressions when key variables are missing or ob-
served only through intervals. Imputation or assumptions about the observation pro-
cess can yield seemingly precise but misleading conclusions. We develop methods for
identification and inference that remain robust to such incomplete data. For a broad
class of conditional moment models, we characterize the sharp identified set, the set
of all parameter values consistent with the observed data and maintained regression
model, without restricting how incomplete observations arise. We establish Hausdorff-
consistent estimation and uniformly valid confidence regions, and develop computa-

relating interval-elicited discount rates to on-time high-school graduation, conventional
inference excludes zero, whereas our interval-data-robust confidence regions include it.
Exploiting sharp identification nevertheless yields substantially tighter confidence re-
gions than non-sharp alternatives.

# Inference After Model Refutation: Uniform Post-Relaxation Inference for Partially Identified Models  
Ulrich Hounyo  
[econ.EM](https://arcxiv.org/category/econ.EM)arXiv:2611.15552
## Abstract  
When data reject an econometric model, the researcher must decide which identifying assumptions to give up. If several equally preferred repairs restore compatibility, the repair itself is unknown, and inference under any one of them can exclude structural values supported by the others, even when that inference is exact. I propose Post-Relaxation Projection (PR), which carries one simultaneous confidence event through every repair that may be minimal. With repair-by-repair primitive bounds, PR equals the union of all post-relaxation targets compatible with the band, so no smaller band-based set has the same guarantee. I derive limits on learning the repair, the exact perturbation radius of the minimal-repair correspondence, oracle-equivalent adaptation, and a reduced-form version valid at zero first stages. In cross-country data on institutions and income, the data do not settle which historical instrument should be dropped, yet every admissible minimum repair implies a positive effect of institutions.

Title: Indirect inference in incomplete and partially identified econometric models

Authors: Lixiong Li, Marc Henry

View PDF HTML (experimental)

Abstract: We extend the indirect inference principle to structural econometric models that are incomplete, in the sense that a single value of the structural parameter may be compatible with multiple distributions of the observed endogenous variables, so that the structural parameter is typically only partially identified. We define the binding function as the smallest norm of the auxiliary estimating equations over the set of data generating processes compatible with the structural model. Hence, we obtain a confidence region by inverting a test of the hypothesis that the binding function vanishes at the pseudo-true value. A dual characterization based on random set theory makes the binding function computationally tractable. We define the auxiliary model conditionally on the covariates to remove its dependence on the unknown covariate distribution and we show that the binding function is Lipschitz and Hadamard directionally differentiable, so that the numerical delta method delivers valid critical values. We show that the method provides significant computational advantages without relinquishing informativeness in a simulation experiment based on an entry game with 100 potential entrants.

## Abstract

When data reject an econometric model, the researcher must decide which identifying assumptions to give up. If several equally preferred repairs restore compatibility, the repair itself is unknown, and inference under any one of them can exclude structural values supported by the others, even when that inference is exact. I propose Post-Relaxation Projection (PR), which carries one simultaneous confidence event through every repair that may be minimal. With repair-by-repair primitive bounds, PR equals the union of all post-relaxation targets compatible with the band, so no smaller band-based set has the same guarantee. I derive limits on learning the repair, the exact perturbation radius of the minimal-repair correspondence, oracle-equivalent adaptation, and a reduced-form version valid at zero first stages. In cross-country data on institutions and income, the data do not settle which historical instrument should be dropped, yet every admissible minimum repair implies a positive effect of institutions.

The paper introduces **Post-Relaxation Projection (PR)** , a uniform inference framework for partially identified models where researchers must select a "repair" to address model rejection (e.g., dropping invalid instruments or moment inequalities). When multiple repairs are equally plausible _ex ante_ , choosing a single one is statistically invalid because the selection process itself is subject to sampling uncertainty, potentially leading to the exclusion of structural values that would be supported by other equally minimal, feasible repairs.

PR avoids the "select-then-infer" trap by constructing a simultaneous confidence event that covers all potential repairs. Instead of selecting one repair, PR retains every candidate repair whose feasibility is consistent with the data-driven bounds.

In brief

Policy simulations built on models of repeated decisions — whether a factory keeps operating, whether a firm exports — normally need assumptions researchers cannot defend, such as that a closing firm's assets are worth nothing. What can be learned without them? This paper shows the answer is a range rather than a single number, computable even with large numbers of possible situations, and often narrow enough to sign the policy effect. In one example the data actually reject the zero-scrap-value convention. Revisiting a study of Colombian exporters, the original ranking of subsidies survives weaker assumptions but hinges on one. Why it matters: precise-looking results may rest on untested conventions.

## What this paper finds — and why it matters

**Research Question.** Discrete choice data identify only *differences* in agents’ utilities, not utility levels. # A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends∗

### Ashesh Rambachan† Jonathan Roth‡ April 1, 2022

Abstract This paper proposes tools for robust inference in difference-in-differences and eventstudy designs where the parallel trends assumption may be violated. Instead of requiring that parallel trends holds exactly, we impose restrictions on how different the post-treatment violations of parallel trends can be from the pre-treatment differences in trends ("pre-trends"). The causal parameter of interest is partially identified under these restrictions. We introduce two approaches that guarantee uniformly valid inference under the imposed restrictions, and we derive novel results showing that they have desirable power properties in our context. We illustrate how economic knowledge can inform the restrictions on the possible violations of parallel trends in two economic applications. We also highlight how our approach can be used to conduct sensitivity analyses showing what causal conclusions can be drawn under various restrictions on the possible violations of the parallel trends assumption. Keywords: Difference-in-differences, event-study, parallel trends, robust inference, sensitivity analysis, partial identification.

seltz.snippet:
This paper proposes a bootstrap-based procedure to build confidence intervals for single components of a partially identified parameter vector, and for smooth functions of such components, in moment (in)equality models. The extreme points of our confidence interval are obtained by maximizing/minimizing the value of the component (or function) of interest subject to the sample analog of the moment (in)equality conditions properly relaxed. The novelty is that the amount of relaxation, or critical level, is computed so that the component (or function) of θ , instead of θ itself, is uniformly asymptotically covered with prespecied probability. Calibration of the critical level is based on repeatedly checking feasibility of linear programming problems, rendering it computationally attractive. Computation of the extreme points of the confidence interval is based on a novel application of the response surface method for global optimization, which may prove of independent interest also for applications of other methods of inference in the moment (in)equalities literature.

The critical level is by construction smaller (in finite sample) than the one used if projecting confience regions designed to cover the entire parameter vector . In statistics and econometrics, **set identification** (or **partial identification**) extends the concept of identifiability (or "point identification") in statistical models to environments where the model and the distribution of observable variables are not sufficient to determine a unique value for the model parameters, but instead constrain the parameters to lie in a strict subset of the parameter space. Statistical models that are set (or partially) identified arise in a variety of settings in economics, including game theory and the Rubin causal model. Unlike approaches that deliver point-identification of the model parameters, methods from the literature on partial identification are used to obtain set estimates that are valid under weaker modelling assumptions.

## History

Early works containing the main ideas of set identification included Frisch (1934) and Marschak & Andrews (1944). However, the methods were significantly developed and promoted by Charles Manski, beginning with Manski (1989) and Manski (1990).

We propose a bootstrap-based calibrated projection procedure to build confidence intervals for single components and for smooth functions of a partially identified parameter vector in moment (in)equality models. The method controls asymptotic coverage uniformly over a large class of data generating processes.  
The extreme points of the calibrated projection confidence interval are obtained by extremizing the value of the component (or function) of interest subject to a proper relaxation of studentized sample analogs of the moment (in)equality conditions. The degree of relaxation, or critical level, is calibrated so that the component (or function) of , not itself, is uniformly asymptotically covered with prespecied probability. This calibration is based on repeatedly checking feasibility of linear programming problems, rendering it computationally attractive.  
Nonetheless, the program defining an extreme point of the confidence interval is generally nonlinear and potentially intricate. We provide an algorithm, based on the response surface method for global optimization, that approximates the solution rapidly and accurately. The algorithm is of independent interest for inference on optimal values of stochastic nonlinear programs. We establish its convergence under conditions satisfied by canonical examples in the moment (in)equalities literature.  
Our assumptions and those used in the leading alternative approach (a profiling based method) are not nested. An extensive Monte Carlo analysis conrms the accuracy of the solution algorithm and the good statistical as well as computational performance of calibrated projection, including in comparison to other methods.

This paper examines a general class of inferential problems in semiparametric and nonparametric models defined by conditional moment restrictions. We construct tests for the hypothesis that at least one element of the identified set satisfies a conjectured (Banach space) “equality” and/or (a Banach lattice) “inequality” constraint. # Inference After Model Refutation:
Uniform Post-Relaxation Inference for Partially Identified Models
This version: November 11, 2026
###### Abstract
When data reject a model, the researcher must decide which identifying assumptions to give up. If several equally preferred repairs restore compatibility, the repair itself is unknown, and inference under any one of them can exclude structural values supported by the others. I propose Post-Relaxation Projection (PR), which carries one simultaneous confidence event through every repair that may be minimal. For a rectangular band on the repair-specific restrictions, PR contains exactly the post-relaxation targets compatible with that band. I also derive limits on learning the repair, its exact perturbation radius, oracle-equivalent adaptation, and versions for instrumental variables without a first-stage relevance bound. In cross-country data on institutions and income, the data do not settle which historical instrument to drop, yet every admissible minimum repair implies a positive effect, and the sign survives sizable direct effects of the instruments on income.

Empirical work rarely stops when a maintained model is rejected. The usual response is to weaken it: drop an exclusion restriction, remove a block of moment inequalities, or relax a shape or behavioral restriction. This step is innocuous when one relaxation is clearly the right one. It is not innocuous when several relaxations are judged equally costly on substantive grounds, each is just enough to restore compatibility with the data, and they support different values of the structural parameter. Choosing among them then changes the object being estimated, not only the estimator. In this paper each repair is a candidate relaxation written down before the sample is examined, the repairs are ranked by a scientific order fixed in advance, and the post-refutation target is built from every minimum feasible repair.

ultimate.title: Weak-Instrument Inference and Model Diagnostics in Double Machine Learning for Linear Instrumental Variable Models
ultimate.snippet: We study weak-instrument-robust inference in partially linear instrumental-variables models with learned nuisances. Building on an i.i.d. uniform-size baseline, we establish uniform asymptotic validity of clustered cross-fitted Anderson–Rubin inference and cross-fitted score inference under the stated sampling and nuisance-rate conditions. Extensions establish Anderson–Rubin validity for survey-weighted target laws and fold-nested generated instruments. A supporting population benchmark shows that prediction-optimal instrument residualization maximizes concentration when the treatment nuisance is correctly specified. A five-design diagnostic portfolio, a known-truth Monte Carlo, and an exploratory selector examine how nuisance specification and estimation affect realized strength and inference.

ultimate.title: Post-Selection Inference for Partially Identified Parameters
ultimate.snippet:
Post-Selection Inference for Partially Identified Parameters∗
Sukjin Han†
Adam McCloskey‡
November 16, 2026
Abstract
Partial identification of parameters such as average treatment effects, average partial
effects and welfare is particularly common when using observational data and experimental
data with imperfect compliance due to the endogeneity of individuals’ treatment uptake.
In this setting, the researcher is typically interested in a treatment or policy that is either
selected from the estimated set of best-performers or arises from a data-dependent selection
rule. In this paper, we develop new inference tools for partially-identified parameters chosen
via these forms of selection. We develop three types of confidence intervals for data-dependent
and partially-identified parameters, discuss how they apply to several examples of interest
and prove their uniform asymptotic validity under weak assumptions.

ultimate.title: Model-Agnostic Covariate-Assisted Inference on Partially Identified Causal Effects
ultimate.snippet: Many causal estimands are only partially identifiable since they depend on the unobservable joint distribution between potential outcomes. Stratification on pretreatment covariates can yield sharper partial identification bounds; however, unless the covariates are discrete with relatively small support, this approach typically requires consistent estimation of the conditional distributions of the potential outcomes given the covariates. Thus, existing approaches may fail under model misspecification or if consistency assumptions are violated. In this study, we propose a unified and model-agnostic inferential approach for a wide class of partially identified estimands, based on duality theory for optimal transport problems. In randomized experiments, our approach can wrap around any estimates of the conditional distributions and provide uniformly valid inference, even if the initial estimates are arbitrarily inaccurate. Also, our approach is doubly robust in observational studies. Notably, this property allows analysts to use the multiplier bootstrap to select covariates and models without sacrificing validity even if the true model is not included. Furthermore, if the conditional distributions are estimated at semiparametric rates, our approach matches the performance of an oracle with perfect knowledge of the outcome model. Finally, we propose an efficient computational framework, enabling implementation on many practical problems in causal inference.

ultimate.title: Sharp Identification for Regression with Interval-Observed and Missing Covariates
ultimate.snippet:
Researchers frequently estimate regressions when key variables are missing or ob-
served only through intervals. Imputation or assumptions about the observation pro-
cess can yield seemingly precise but misleading conclusions. We develop methods for
identification and inference that remain robust to such incomplete data. For a broad
class of conditional moment models, we characterize the sharp identified set, the set
of all parameter values consistent with the observed data and maintained regression
model, without restricting how incomplete observations arise. We establish Hausdorff-
consistent estimation and uniformly valid confidence regions, and develop computa-
tionally tractable implementations for common regression models. In an application
relating interval-elicited discount rates to on-time high-school graduation, conventional
inference excludes zero, whereas our interval-data-robust confidence regions include it.
Exploiting sharp identification nevertheless yields substantially tighter confidence re-
gions than non-sharp alternatives.

ultimate.title: Nonparametric Bayesian Inference for Partially Identified Discrete Response Models
ultimate.snippet: This paper proposes a nonparametric Bayesian inference framework for partially identified discrete response models. The key observation is that these models map a reduced-form conditional choice probability to an identified set. Consequently, nonparametric Bayesian inference for the conditional probability mass function leads to Bayesian inference for the identified set. The inference framework nests conditional moment inequalities and linear systems with unknown coefficients as special cases. We show that the posterior is consistent for the true identified set when the model is correctly specified, show that the posterior can consistently detect model misspecification, and show posterior consistency for a pseudo-identified set that is valid under misspecification. We also verify the assumptions for a class of priors based on Gaussian processes that we use to implement our proposal. webiq.snippet:
该论文提出了一种名为**后放松投影（Post-Relaxation Projection, PR）**的推理方法，旨在解决当数据拒绝原模型时，研究者因存在多种同等合理的“修复”（Relaxation）方案而面临的不确定性问题。

在实证研究中，若数据拒绝了主模型，研究者通常会选择弱化假设（即“修复”模型）。如果存在多种先验上同样合理的修复方案（如排除不同的工具变量或矩条件），且每种方案都能使模型与数据兼容，但这些方案对应的结构参数识别集不同，那么“选择一个修复方案再进行推理”的做法会导致失效。论文指出，这种选择步骤本身就是一种不含在目标参数中的约束，会造成严重的推断偏差。

PR方法的核心思想是：不进行任何预先的修复选择，而是通过一个 联合置信事件 覆盖所有可能的最小修复方案。

构建一个关于原始模型参数的同时置信矩形（Simultaneous Primitive Band），涵盖所有修复方案的约束条件及可行性指标 qR (P)q\_R (P)qR​ (P)。 定义可行性“三明治”规则，根据矩形中的可行性指标判断哪些修复方案在统计上仍有可能是人口意义下的“最小修复”。 PR集合即为在置信区域内所有被认为符合“最小修复”条件的方案所对应的结构外集（Structural Outer Sets）的并集。


- **信息界限**：作者证明了在局部错定模型下，任何诚实的推理过程都存在一个关于学习最小修复方案的极小极大风险界限。PR方法能够通过矩形信息直接获得目标集的覆盖，且无需估计具体的修复方案。
**Bandwise Completeness**：在 canonical 构造下，PR集合恰好是所有与该置信矩形相容的最小修复目标的并集，这意味着该方法在给定的矩形信息下达到了信息最优。
**弱工具变量（Weak IV）适应性**：在工具变量模型中，该方法不需要第一阶段相关性（First-stage relevance）的下界，能够在不依赖于第一阶段系数比率的情况下，实现对结构参数的均匀有效覆盖。
**分辨率自适应（Resolution Adaptation）**：论文进一步提出了一种通过独立试点样本（Pilot Sample）来加速修复方案识别的方法。当可行性边界的间距足够大时，该过程在渐进意义上等价于已知的“先知（Oracle）”推理。

PR方法显示，无论放弃哪一个工具变量，只要遵循“最小修复”原则，制度对收入的正向影响在合理的直接效应干扰容限内都是稳健的。

**Local Adaptation Bound:** 국소적 대안 (local alternatives) 하에서 특정 파라미터 값이 타겟에서 제외될 확률에 대한 하한을 제시합니다. 이는 LAN (Local Asymptotic Normality) 조건을 기반으로 하며, 어떤 절차도 정보의 한계를 넘어서는 추론을 할 수 없음을 보여줍니다.
**Resolution-Adaptive Inference:** 표본 분할 (data splitting)을 통해 pilot sample에서 복구 전략이 충분히 분리될 경우, 점근적으로 오라클 (oracle) 추론과 동일한 성능을 발휘하도록 하는 해상도 적응형 추론 방식을 제안합니다.

본 논문은 Rodrik, Subramanian, and Trebbi (2002; 2004)의 국가 제도와 소득 데이터에 PR을 적용하였습니다. 데이터가 어떤 역사적 도구 변수를 제외해야 할지 결정하지 못하는 상황에서도, 모든 최소 복구 전략이 제도와 소득 간의 양 (+)의 관계를 지지함을 입증하였습니다. 특히, 첫 번째 단계 (first-stage)가 약한 경우 (weak instrument)에도 추가적인 가정이 필요 없는 강건한 추론이 가능함을 보였습니다.
